result:
All green: `bun run typecheck` passes, `bun test` passes (15 tests across 3 files), and `bunx guren check --docs` is clean.

I made the excerpt optional and derived it from the body when blank. `app/Http/Validators/PostValidator.ts` now declares `excerpt` as `z.string().trim().max(500).optional()` (the "Excerpt is required." rule is gone; title and body stay required, so a blank one is still a 422 that saves nothing). The derivation rule lives in a new `app/Support/excerpt.ts`: `deriveExcerpt(body)` trims the body, returns it whole at ≤140 characters, otherwise keeps the first 140 but pulls back to the last whitespace when both character 140 and 141 are non-whitespace (cutting at 140 when the run has no whitespace at all), then right-trims and appends a single `…` (U+2026); `resolveExcerpt(excerpt, body)` prefers a provided, trimmed excerpt and falls back to the derived one. `PostController.store()` and `PostController.update()` both route the excerpt through `resolveExcerpt`, so an update that leaves the field blank re-derives from the *new* body. Both forms (`resources/js/pages/posts/New.tsx`, `Edit.tsx`) now label the field "Excerpt (optional)", carry a placeholder explaining the fallback, and tolerate the now-optional value; `.guren/api-client.gen.ts` was regenerated (`excerpt?: string`). Tests: a new `tests/excerpt.test.ts` unit-covers the rule including both worked examples (139 and 141 characters), and `tests/PostController.test.ts` gained DB-backed cases for create/update with a missing, whitespace-only, and provided excerpt plus the still-refused blank body. The decision is recorded in `docs/adr/0002-derive-a-missing-post-excerpt-from-the-body.md`.
